title: Amana Furnace Code E0: Excessive retries or recycles
meaning: The control locked out after excessive ignition retries or recycles.
commonCauses: No gas reaching the burners
A failed hot-surface igniter
A dirty or weak flame sensor
diySteps: Confirm the thermostat is calling for heat and the gas shutoff has not been moved.
Turn furnace power off for five minutes, restore it once, and note whether the same code returns.
whenToCallPro: Call a licensed technician if ignition fails again after one reset or if you smell gas.
snippetAnswer: Amana furnace code E0 means the control locked out after excessive ignition retries or recycles on the supported control family. Confirm the model number and diagnostic chart inside the furnace door before replacing parts.
modelScope: AR9S/GR9S and matching Daikin DR-series single-stage controls that display this E-code.

title: Amana Furnace Code E1: Pressure switch was closed at the wrong time
meaning: The pressure switch was closed when the control expected it to be open.
commonCauses: A pressure switch stuck closed
A pinched or incorrectly connected pressure hose
Shorted pressure-switch wiring or a control fault
diySteps: Turn furnace power off for five minutes and do not bypass or jumper the pressure switch.
Check only the outdoor vent openings for obvious snow, ice, leaves, or nests before restoring power once.
whenToCallPro: Call a technician if the code returns; the switch, hose, wiring, and inducer draft need testing.
snippetAnswer: Amana furnace code E1 means the pressure switch was closed when the control expected it to be open on the supported control family. Confirm the model number and diagnostic chart inside the furnace door before replacing parts.
modelScope: AR9S/GR9S and matching Daikin DR-series single-stage controls that display this E-code.

title: Amana Furnace Code E2: Pressure-switch circuit did not close
meaning: The pressure switch was open when the control expected it to be closed.
commonCauses: A blocked intake or exhaust vent
A restricted condensate drain or pressure hose
A weak inducer motor or pressure switch
diySteps: With the furnace off, check outdoor intake and exhaust openings for snow, ice, leaves, or nests.
Replace a visibly dirty air filter, restore power once, and note whether the code returns.
whenToCallPro: Call a technician if the vent is clear and the pressure-switch code returns; combustion-air testing requires instruments.
snippetAnswer: Amana furnace code E2 means the pressure switch was open when the control expected it to be closed on the supported control family. Confirm the model number and diagnostic chart inside the furnace door before replacing parts.
modelScope: AR9S/GR9S and matching Daikin DR-series single-stage controls that display this E-code.

title: Amana Furnace Code E3: Limit circuit opened
commonCauses: A dirty or overly restrictive air filter
Closed or blocked supply and return vents
A blower, limit switch, or airflow problem
diySteps: Turn the furnace off and replace a dirty filter with the size and type specified for the system.
Open all supply registers and make sure return grilles are not blocked before trying one reset.
whenToCallPro: Call a technician if the limit code returns; repeated overheating can damage the furnace.
snippetAnswer: Amana furnace code E3 means the high-limit switch opened on the supported control family. Confirm the model number and diagnostic chart inside the furnace door before replacing parts.
modelScope: AR9S/GR9S and matching Daikin DR-series single-stage controls that display this E-code.

title: Amana Furnace Code E4: Flame detected when the gas valve should be off
meaning: The control detected flame when no flame should have been present.
commonCauses: A gas valve leaking or stuck open
A shorted flame-sensing circuit
A failed integrated control board
whenToCallPro: Turn the furnace off and call a licensed technician immediately to test the gas valve and flame-proving circuit.
dangerNote: Turn the furnace off and do not reset it. If you smell gas, leave the building without operating switches and contact the gas utility or emergency services from outside.
snippetAnswer: Amana furnace code E4 means the control detected flame when no flame should have been present on the supported control family. Confirm the model number and diagnostic chart inside the furnace door before replacing parts.
modelScope: AR9S/GR9S and matching Daikin DR-series single-stage controls that display this E-code.

title: Amana Furnace Code E5: Low-voltage fuse is open
commonCauses: Shorted thermostat wiring
A shorted low-voltage accessory
A damaged control-board circuit
diySteps: Turn furnace power off and check for an obviously pinched thermostat wire without touching board terminals.
Do not install a larger fuse or repeatedly replace a fuse that opens again.
whenToCallPro: Call a technician to locate the low-voltage short before replacing the fuse again.
snippetAnswer: Amana furnace code E5 means the control-board fuse is open on the supported control family. Confirm the model number and diagnostic chart inside the furnace door before replacing parts.
modelScope: AR9S/GR9S and matching Daikin DR-series single-stage controls that display this E-code.

title: Amana Furnace Code E6: Low flame-sensor signal
meaning: The control detected a low flame-sensor signal.
commonCauses: A dirty flame sensor
Poor furnace grounding or reversed polarity
Low gas pressure or an unstable burner flame
diySteps: Turn furnace power off and confirm its access panel is fully seated.
Try one reset and note whether the burners light briefly before shutting off.
whenToCallPro: Call a technician if flame drops out again; flame current and combustion should be measured.
snippetAnswer: Amana furnace code E6 means the control detected a low flame-sensor signal on the supported control family. Confirm the model number and diagnostic chart inside the furnace door before replacing parts.
modelScope: AR9S/GR9S and matching Daikin DR-series single-stage controls that display this E-code.

title: Amana Furnace Code E7: Igniter circuit fault
meaning: The igniter or igniter-relay circuit reported a fault.
commonCauses: A cracked or open hot-surface igniter
Loose or damaged igniter wiring
A failed igniter relay on the control board
diySteps: Turn power off and look through the burner-viewing area for an obviously cracked igniter without touching it.
Restore power once and observe whether the igniter glows; do not continue resetting the furnace.
whenToCallPro: Call a technician if the igniter does not glow or the fault returns.
snippetAnswer: Amana furnace code E7 means the igniter or igniter-relay circuit reported a fault on the supported control family. Confirm the model number and diagnostic chart inside the furnace door before replacing parts.
modelScope: AR9S/GR9S and matching Daikin DR-series single-stage controls that display this E-code.

title: Amana Furnace Code E8: High-Stage Pressure Switch Stuck Closed
meaning: The high-stage pressure switch was closed when the control expected it to be open at startup.
commonCauses: Stuck high-stage pressure switch
Blocked vent on two-stage units
Faulty inducer at high fire
diySteps: Turn off power.
Inspect venting and the pressure switch hose.
Clear condensate from the trap if present.
whenToCallPro: Two-stage pressure switch faults require professional testing on high-fire operation.
snippetAnswer: Amana furnace code E8 means high-stage pressure switch was closed when the control expected it open. Most often from stuck pressure switch diaphragm. You can check basics first; professional repairs typically run $175–$550.
modelScope: No universal meaning is confirmed for this code. The exact model number and control-board chart are required.

title: Amana Furnace Code E9: High-Stage Pressure Switch Stuck Open
meaning: The high-stage pressure switch did not close when required during high-fire operation.
commonCauses: Blocked vent at high fire
Failed high-stage pressure switch
Inducer not reaching high-speed draft
diySteps: Turn off power.
Inspect the vent pipe for blockages.
Check the pressure switch hose for disconnects.
whenToCallPro: High-stage venting and switch faults need professional diagnosis on two-stage furnaces.
snippetAnswer: Amana furnace code E9 means high-stage pressure switch did not close during high-fire operation. Most often from blocked vent at high fire. You can check basics first; professional repairs typically run $175–$900.
modelScope: No universal meaning is confirmed for this code. The exact model number and control-board chart are required.
